name: Raghu Seshabhattar

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Raghu Seshabhattar writes poetry and literary essays in Telugu. His books include Sourabham, a collection of literary essays published by Astra Publishers, and the poetry collection Analpam. A published translation of his work places his early life in Khammam and his professional life in Hyderabad. Kabita Live presents his poem “Swing” in Elanaaga’s English translation.

“Swing” treats sight as an imaginative act: eyes do more than observe the world; they tend dreams and set them in motion. Shepherds, antelopes, an ancient goddess and temple bells carry the poem between the outer landscape and inward experience. Its recurring swing gathers memory and changing time into a gentle movement, while imagined vision takes precedence over outward signs of power.
